title: The Old King Is Cold
body: Your father is three days dead, and already the court watches to see what kind of ruler you will be. Your first act as king will be remembered.

choices.text: Open the treasury for a lavish coronation feast
Forgo the feast — the realm's coin is not for pomp
Pardon the prisoners in your father's dungeons

title: Refugees from the Steppe
body: A ragged column of nomads — mothers, elders, hard-eyed horsemen — reaches your border, fleeing the very Horde that darkens your own horizon. They kneel and beg for refuge.

choices.text: Shelter them — their riders know the Horde's ways
Turn them away; you have troubles enough
Seize all they have and sell them — the steppe owes you

title: Strangers in the Halls
body: The nomads have wintered among your people. Their scouts already map the Horde's outriders, and their smiths teach your riders the recurve bow — but your lords grumble at strangers seated at their tables.

choices.text: Arm them as auxiliaries and ride with them
Keep them fed, but apart
Now winter's past, expel them

title: Blood Money
body: The nomads you sold made your coffers heavy — and made you an enemy. Word reached the khan that this realm trades the desperate for coin, and the Horde now rides with a grudge. But you are rich, and gold buys many things.

choices.text: Pour the plunder into tribute — buy the khan's mercy
Raise a Grand Host with the coin
Pocket it; the walls will hold

title: The Tax Collector's Smile
body: Your coffers are thin. The collector waits with his ledger open and suggests, gently, that the peasants might bear a little more.

choices.text: Raise taxes
Spare the peasants

title: The Foreign Caravan
body: Eastern merchants spread silk and spice before the throne — and ask, between courtesies, how your walls are manned.

choices.text: Trade freely
Tax them heavily
Rob them, blame bandits

title: The Steppe Envoy
body: A rider from the khan's court arrives bearing gifts and thinly veiled threats.

choices.text: Honour him lavishly
Repay his veiled threats with open insult

title: The Dancing Plague
body: A woman has danced for six days. Forty have joined her. Physicians prescribe more dancing.

choices.text: Build them a stage
Declare it demonic
Charge admission

title: The War on Cats
body: A papal letter declares the cat an agent of Satan. The rats are delighted.

choices.text: Enforce the purge
Quietly protect the cats
Tax cat-owners for consorting with the Devil

title: A Bountiful Harvest
body: The granaries overflow. The bishop suggests gratitude is best expressed in coin.

choices.text: Tithe generously
Keep it all

title: The Long Winter
body: Snow buries the roads. In the villages they have begun to eat the seed corn.

choices.text: Open the granary
Let the weak perish

title: Your Brother's Ambition
body: Your younger brother has been asking questions about the succession — and asking them at tables that have never been friendly to you.

choices.text: Have him drowned
Marry him off abroad
Trust him

title: The Caravan's Revenge
body: The merchants you robbed have returned, and they have hired swords.

choices.text: Pay them off
Put them to the sword

title: The Holy War
body: The Pope preaches holy war against a neighbour whose lands are rich and whose sins, on inspection, prove sufficient.

choices.text: Answer the call, plunder
Send coin, stay home
Refuse the Pope

title: A Heretic in the Square
body: A preacher insists the meek shall inherit the earth. The bishop finds this teaching dangerous to the tithe.

choices.text: Burn him for the glory of God
Tax his followers instead
Let him speak; smile politely

title: A Plague Among the Swine
body: Disease thins the herds. The physician blames miasma, the priest blames sin, the peasants blame you.

choices.text: Fund a quarantine
Declare a day of repentance
Burn a witch to calm the mob

title: The Mercenary's Bill
body: The sellswords want paying. They are very large, and they are standing in your hall.

choices.text: Pay in full
Pay in titles and honors
Don't pay; hope they leave

title: The Mercenaries Help Themselves
body: Unpaid and unbothered, the sellswords are pillaging the countryside to collect their own wages.

choices.text: Let them take their due
Pay them off, twice over, to leave
Hunt them down

title: A Marriage of Convenience
body: A neighboring lord offers his daughter, a fat dowry, and a lucrative trade road.

choices.text: Accept the match
Haggle for a bigger dowry
Marry for love instead

title: The Relic Salesman
body: A friar sells you the actual finger bone of a saint. Remarkably, he has three more.

choices.text: Buy it; display it proudly
Expose him as a fraud
Buy all four; make the town a pilgrim shrine

title: The Pilgrim Road Pays
body: Pilgrims queue for miles to kiss four suspiciously similar finger bones. The collection plate runneth over.

choices.text: Collect the profits
Redirect the takings to the poor

title: Bandits on the Trade Road
body: Your one profitable road is being taxed by men who hold no charter from you.

choices.text: Send soldiers to clear them
Hire the bandits as tax men
Ignore it

title: The Cleared Road Pays Tolls
body: With the bandits gone, merchants flow freely again, and gladly pay for the privilege.

choices.text: Collect the tolls
Share the toll with the militia

title: The Famine Decree
body: Grain is scarce. There is enough for the court, or enough for the city. Not both.

choices.text: Feed the people; the court goes hungry
Feed the court; sell the surplus high
Throw a feast to put a brave face on hunger

title: A Saint's Vision
body: A peasant girl says God speaks to her, and that He is displeased with your taxes.

choices.text: Canonize her; gently redirect the visions
Imprison her as a fraud
Martyr her quietly

title: The Cult of the Martyr
body: The girl you silenced has become a saint in the streets, and her believers are no longer quiet.

choices.text: Suppress the cult
Co-opt it; declare a holy day

title: The Cadaver Synod
body: The new Pope has dug up his predecessor, dressed the corpse in full regalia, and put it on trial for heresy.

choices.text: Endorse the spectacle
Mock it from afar
Send a sober envoy to lend dignity

title: Precedent Comes Due
body: A rival faction, citing the precedent you endorsed, proposes to try your own rule in absentia. It is, they insist, only fair.

choices.text: Ignore the mummery
Publicly rebut the charges
Have the mockers arrested

title: The War of the Bucket
body: Soldiers of a rival city have stolen a wooden bucket from your town well. It is, by any honest measure, a bucket.

choices.text: March to war over the bucket
Let it go; you own other buckets
Demand a humiliating ransom for its return

title: The Bucket War Drags On
body: Years on, the war over a wooden pail has cost more than the treasury it hangs in. Neither side will blink first.

choices.text: Sue for peace
Press the siege

title: The King of Glass
body: A fellow monarch is convinced his body is made of glass. He has iron rods sewn into his clothes and begs your discreet counsel.

choices.text: Send sympathy and your best physician
Spread the tale to weaken his crown
Press your claim on his lands while he's mad

title: A Crown Made of Glass Shatters
body: The rumors you spread took root. The glass king's own nobles have moved against him, and his realm is up for the taking.

choices.text: Seize the opportunity
Stay above it

title: The Glass King's Lands
body: The claim you pressed while he raved has quietly become fact. The annexed revenue arrives on schedule.

choices.text: Collect the annexed revenue
Grant it to the church instead

title: The Pig on Trial
body: A pig stands accused of murdering a child. It has been arrested, jailed, and assigned a lawyer mounting a spirited defense.

choices.text: Hold a solemn trial and hang the pig
Pardon it; it's a pig
Try the owner instead and seize his farm

title: The White Ship
body: Your heir and the court's young nobles have seized the finest ship for a wine-drunk midnight crossing. The harbor-master begs you to forbid it.

choices.text: Forbid the voyage
Let youth be young
Forgive the folly — but sail with them to keep order

title: The White Ship's Wake
body: The ship struck a rock in the dark. The court is in mourning, the succession thrown into doubt, and the sea keeps its secrets.

choices.text: Mourn publicly; name a new heir
Blame the drunken captain and move on

title: The Flagellants
body: A procession of penitents winds through your streets, whipping themselves bloody to beg God to lift the plague.

choices.text: Join them; flog yourself publicly
Ban them as a public nuisance
Sell them penance permits

title: The Golden Nose
body: A warlord your forebears once deposed and mutilated has returned at the head of an army, wearing a nose of solid gold and a grudge older than your reign.

choices.text: Pay him off lavishly
Meet him in battle
Offer marriage and a title

title: The Battle for the Throne
body: Steel has decided what diplomacy could not. Word of the field reaches the court before the dust does.

choices.text: Claim victory; parade the gold nose
Sue for terms after heavy losses
Strip the fallen for coin and steel

title: The Children's Crusade
body: A shepherd boy preaches that God has chosen the children to retake the Holy Land through purity alone. Thousands are massing to march.

choices.text: Forbid the march; send the children home to their mothers
Bless and fund the crusade
Sell the pilgrims passage on ships

title: The Crusade That Wasn't
body: The sea did not part. Word trickles back of a march that ended in starvation and slave markets, and the bishop who blessed it is asked hard questions.

choices.text: Blame the shepherd boy
Fund masses for the dead

title: The Tax on Windows
body: Your treasurer proposes taxing the things people cannot hide: beards, windows, the colour purple.

choices.text: Tax beards and windows
Tax only noble luxuries
Refuse — the crown does not hound its people

title: The Relic Auction
body: Your monasteries are in a bidding war over a saint's shinbone, a vial of holy tears, and a feather from the Angel Gabriel.

choices.text: Tax the relic trade
Charge a royal fee to authenticate relics
Denounce the whole trade as blasphemy

title: The Goat Bone Scandal
body: A relic you personally authenticated has been identified, definitively, as a goat bone. The bishop is not amused.

choices.text: Deny it; double down
Publicly apologize and refund the faithful

title: The Rat Plague
body: With the cats gone, the rats have inherited the granaries, and brought a fever with them.

choices.text: Fund a quarantine
Quietly reintroduce cats

title: The Spymaster's Ledger
body: Your Wren lays a ledger of rivals' secrets on the table and awaits your pleasure.

choices.text: Blackmail them quietly
Burn the ledger; you want no part of it

title: Muster the Levies
body: Your Marshal proposes a disciplined muster, fit only for a ruler who has led men before.

choices.text: Lead the muster yourself
Let the Marshal handle it
Hire sellswords to fill the ranks
Skip it this year

title: The Marshal's Defection
body: Your Marshal, unpaid too long, has taken half the garrison with him, to the enemy.

choices.text: Purge the disloyal ranks
Buy back their loyalty

title: The Steward Vanishes
body: Your Steward has fled in the night, with the tax ledgers, and no small amount of coin.

choices.text: Launch an inquiry
Let it go; appoint a replacement

title: The Priest's Excommunication
body: Your Court Priest, spurned once too often, denounces you from the pulpit as unfit before God.

choices.text: Silence him
Make a public penance

title: The Spymaster Turns
body: The Wren you starved of coin has sold your secrets to a rival court.

choices.text: Purge the informants
Sue for quiet terms

title: The Scholar's Betrayal
body: Your Scholar, ignored and unpaid, has taken your library's secrets to a rival patron.

choices.text: Denounce the theft publicly
Quietly rebuild the library

title: The Silk Charter
body: Eastern factors propose a standing silk road through your marches — rich, and perilously close to the steppe.

choices.text: Fund the caravanserai and open the road
Take a one-time toll and wave them through
Refuse; the road runs too near the horde

title: The River Guild
body: The barge guilds petition to dredge the river and run regular trade — steady coin, if you fund the works.

choices.text: Charter the guild and open the river
Tax the fords as they are
The river serves the realm free; leave it

title: The Salt Harbor
body: A shipwright offers to build a harbor and open the salt coast to sea trade — profit that rides the same tides as the plague.

choices.text: Build the harbor and open the coast
Sell the license to a merchant house
Decline; the sea brings more than salt

title: A Rival's Embargo
body: A neighboring crown, nursing an old grudge, closes its markets and leans on yours to fall quiet too.

choices.text: Reroute through friendlier ports
Answer embargo with embargo
Swallow the insult and let it pass

title: A Royal Mint
body: Your Steward proposes striking your own coin. A mint of your own would enrich every reign that follows yours — if you can spare the silver to build it.

choices.text: Found the Royal Mint
The old coin serves well enough

title: A Great Cathedral
body: The bishops beg you to raise a cathedral to shame the neighboring realms — a monument that would steady the faithful for generations.

choices.text: Raise the Great Cathedral
Charity serves God better than stone

title: A University
body: Scholars petition for a hall of learning. Its graduates would tutor your heirs for centuries — a costly gift to descendants you will never meet.

choices.text: Charter the University
A prince learns from the saddle, not scrolls

title: The Drunken Baron
body: At the feast, a baron deep in his cups mocks your late father to your face. The hall falls silent, waiting to see what kind of king you are.

choices.text: Have him flogged before the court
Laugh louder than he does, and refill his cup
Pardon him with a cold smile — you are above it

title: The Long Winter's Feast
body: The court grows restless through the dark months. Your Steward counsels a distraction; your confessor, restraint.

choices.text: Throw a feast to outshine the neighbors
Keep a plain and pious table
Give the feast's whole cost to the poor

title: The King's Favorite
body: A dazzling newcomer at court has caught your eye, and the whole realm is watching to see whether the crown keeps its head.

choices.text: Take the favorite to your chambers
Keep the flirtation courtly and no more
Give them in marriage to a lord you trust

title: The Bandit Champion
body: A brigand lord has grown bold enough to challenge the crown's own champion to single combat, and the border is watching.

choices.text: Ride out and face him yourself
Send your best knight in your stead
Pay the brigand to slink away
Lead the whole host out and crush them

title: The Royal Library
body: Your Scholar unrolls plans for a great library, hinting its archives could unravel the oldest threats to the realm — for a ruler patient enough to read.

choices.text: Pore over the chronicles of past reckonings
Fund the library and study there yourself
A king has no time for dust and scrolls

title: Know the Coming Storm
body: The Doom gathers on the horizon. Your Scholar proposes sending clever men to learn its weaknesses before it arrives, rather than merely bracing for it.

choices.text: Send scholars to study the enemy
Trust in walls and swords alone

title: The Relic Peddler
body: A travelling merchant offers, for a price, the genuine finger-bone of a saint — the fourth genuine finger of that same saint you have been offered this year.

choices.text: Buy it; the faithful adore a relic
Expose the fraud with a scholar's eye
Commission a whole set of 'relics' to sell

title: The Astronomer's Warning
body: A wild-eyed stargazer bursts into court swearing the heavens foretell ruin, and begs coin for a tower to read them more clearly.

choices.text: Fund his observatory
Burn his charts as devilry
Nod gravely and forget him by supper

title: The Grand Tourney
body: The lords clamor for a tournament — a chance for glory, for gambling, and for the crown to show itself magnificent.

choices.text: Host a lavish tourney
Ride in the lists yourself
Cancel it — the coffers come first

title: The Sick at the Gate
body: A column of the plague-scarred and the leprous has gathered at the gate, begging sanctuary. The guildmasters want them gone; the friars, sheltered.

choices.text: Fund a hospice beyond the walls
Turn them away from the gates
Wash their feet before the whole court

title: The Drunken Confession
body: Deep in his cups, a decorated knight loudly confesses to an old murder — and realizes, far too late, exactly who is listening.

choices.text: Pardon him, for a generous fee
Hang him as the law demands
Pretend you heard nothing

title: A Marriage of States
body: A neighboring crown offers a match: their kin to your line, sealed with a dowry — and a web of obligations dressed up as affection.

choices.text: Accept the match and the dowry
Haggle for a richer settlement
Refuse the match — the crown needs no bride

title: The Miracle Cure
body: A physician of great confidence and no known school offers a tonic he swears will turn aside any pestilence to come.

choices.text: Buy barrels of it for the people
Have your scholars test his claims first
Run him out of town

title: The Mocking Ballad
body: A filthy song of the crown's every failing is sung in every tavern from the capital to the coast, and it will not die.

choices.text: Learn the words and laugh along
Hunt down the balladeer
Pay for a flattering counter-song

title: The Moneylender's Offer
body: A silken banker offers a loan large enough to solve this year's every problem — and to become next year's only one.

choices.text: Take the loan
Decline; debt is a leash
Take it — a cheating banker deserves no repayment

title: The Debt Comes Due
body: The silken banker returns, rather less silken now, with a sum owed that has quietly doubled somewhere in the counting.

choices.text: Pay what is owed
Default, and damn the consequences

title: The Heir's Folly
body: Word comes of your heir, a stolen horse, a bishop's garden, and a truly heroic quantity of wine.

choices.text: Hush it up, at cost
Let the magistrate have them, royal blood or no
Privately, admire the sheer nerve of it

title: The Witch Trial
body: A frightened village drags a widow before you, blaming her for their failed crops and demanding the crown's justice — by which they mean fire.

choices.text: Give the mob its verdict
Demand real evidence first
Take the widow into your household

title: The Bountiful Year
body: For once the rains came kindly and the fields have answered. The realm has a surplus — and everyone has a strong opinion about it.

choices.text: Store the surplus against hard times
Throw open the granaries in celebration
Cut taxes in thanks to the people

title: Raiders at the Marches
body: Horsemen from beyond the marches are testing your border — burning a hamlet, then melting away before the levy can form.

choices.text: Ride with the levy yourself and scatter them
Buy them off with a chest of silver
The walls will hold — leave it

title: The Marches Burn
body: The raids no longer vanish. The marcher lords beg for troops; smoke stands where villages stood a season ago.

choices.text: Muster the levies in force
Pay a far heavier tribute
Let the borderlands fend for themselves

title: A Province Lost
body: A whole province is sacked, and its surviving lords now ride under the raiders' banner. The march is gone — only the price of the lesson remains.

choices.text: Retake it by fire and blood
Abandon the march; a king does not bargain for scraps

title: Whispers of a Coup
body: Your Marshal dines a little too often, and a little too late, with the realm's most disappointed lords.

choices.text: Have the Wren expose the plotters
Buy their loyalty with gold and titles
A king does not flinch at table-gossip

title: The Conspiracy Has a Banner
body: The grumbling has a banner now, and a claimant with a plausible drop of royal blood in his veins.

choices.text: Take the ringleaders' heads; pardon the rest
Summon loyal swords to overawe them
Trust in divine right and do nothing

title: Men in the Corridors
body: Armed men fill the halls outside the throne room. The realm will learn tonight whether you are its king or merely its guest.

choices.text: Stand and fight among your own guardsmen
Slip away — gold will win back what is yours by right

title: A Failing Harvest
body: The spring rains never came. The Steward's granary tallies are written in an increasingly shaky hand.

choices.text: Open the royal stores in good time
Buy grain from foreign factors
The peasants have cried wolf before

title: Bread Riots
body: Famine. Riots in the market towns; mothers hold up hollow-cheeked children at your gate.

choices.text: Emergency relief, whatever it costs
Seize the hoarders' grain and give it to the mob
Let the winter thin the hungry

title: The Hunger Winter
body: Starvation empties whole villages, and fever always walks a step behind hunger. The dead begin to outnumber the ploughs.

choices.text: Beg the Church to open its alms
Endure it, and bury the dead in pits

title: A Rising Heresy
body: A hedge-preacher draws crowds by claiming your priests sell forged keys to Heaven — and that God keeps no court at your chapel.

choices.text: Best them in open debate
Suppress them by force — the Church will thank you
Quietly grant a few of their reforms
Heresy withers if you starve it of attention

title: The Sect Takes Root
body: The sect has its own churches now, its own collectors — and its first martyrs, which is worse than either.

choices.text: Burn the ringleaders; absolve their misled flock
Sign an edict of tolerance
Leave it to the bishops

title: A Realm of Two Faiths
body: Two faiths, two tithes, two armies. The realm has quietly split its soul, and both halves are arming.

choices.text: Wage holy war on your own people
Legitimize the new church — a gift, never a surrender

title: A Rival's Scheme
body: A cousin with an inconveniently good claim has begun smiling at court with the patience of a man who expects to inherit.

choices.text: Smile back, and patiently unpick their web
Marry them off to a cold and distant keep
Let the cousin smile

title: The Claimant Gathers Friends
body: Your cousin now has friends in three provinces, a chest of foreign gold, and a genealogist on retainer.

choices.text: Bribe their friends back to your side
Have the Wren break the plot, then pardon your cousin
Ignore the upstart's theatrics

title: War Between Kin
body: The cousin raises a banner in the west. It is the oldest and ugliest of wars — the kind fought between kin.

choices.text: Crush the pretender in the field
Carve off a duchy to buy peace

title: The River Takes the Low Fields
body: The thaw came all at once. The river has swallowed the low fields, and three villages sit on their rooftops watching the seed grain float away.

choices.text: Send boats, grain, and royal masons
Declare the flood God's judgment on the villages
Buy the drowned land cheap from the desperate

title: The Midsummer Fires
body: On the shortest night the hills burn with bonfires, and the villages dance around them in ways the Church prefers not to see.

choices.text: Join the dancing until dawn
Watch from horseback, then ride home early
Send priests to turn the fires into a saint's vigil

title: The Wolves Come Down
body: Hard cold has driven the wolves out of the high forest. They have taken sheep, then a swineherd, and the villages bar their doors at dusk.

choices.text: Lead the wolf-hunt yourself
Post a bounty on every pelt
Wolves thin only the careless; do nothing

title: The Khan's Tax-Men
body: Riders of the Horde arrive a season early, unarmed and unhurried, to count your herds and granaries for the khan's toll. Their confidence is its own kind of army.

choices.text: Pay the toll with what you wrung from your own villages
Send them home counted, weighed, and empty-handed
Wine them well and plead a poor year

title: The Confessor Knows
body: Your confessor has heard what the court only whispers of you and the chamberlain's wife. He proposes a penance — public enough to be seen, private enough to be survived.

choices.text: Do the penance, barefoot and seen
Keep the sin; pay for new chapel bells
Remind him what befalls talkative priests

title: The Masque of the Dead Kings
body: For the autumn feast the players propose a masque of your ancestors, crowns of gilt paper and all. Half the court finds it splendid; the other half, treason in fancy dress.

choices.text: Let them play, and laugh loudest at your father
Forbid all mockery of the royal dead
Commission it grander, with yourself as the hero

title: The Dowager's Court
body: Your mother has begun holding a court of her own — smaller than yours, and better attended. Petitioners leave her chambers with promises you never made.

choices.text: Honour her counsel and share the petitions
Retire her to a convent, with full ceremony
Win her courtiers back, one flattery at a time

title: The Ordeal by Water
body: Two villages dispute a mill, and both demand the old justice: bind the accused miller and let the river judge him. Your magistrate would rather read the deeds.

choices.text: Let the river judge, as the fathers did
Rule by the deeds and the testimony
Fine both villages for wasting the crown's day
